headline: STATIC Arabia opens at Dhahran Expo with 240 technical papers on plant integrity
deck: Pressure vessels, heat exchangers, tanks and pipelines get their own exhibition because the cost of getting them wrong is measured per hour.
excerpt: The sixth STATIC Arabia opens at Dhahran Expo in Al Khobar on 8 September, expecting more than 5,000 professionals from the energy, oil and gas, petrochemical and power sectors, with 240 technical presentations across 54 sessions.
content:
STATIC Arabia opens at Dhahran Expo in Al Khobar on 8 September for its sixth edition, running to the 10th. The organisers expect more than 5,000 professionals from the energy, oil and gas, petrochemical and power sectors, with more than 240 technical presentations across 54 sessions.

The subject is static equipment: pressure vessels, heat exchangers, tanks and pipelines. It is the half of a process plant that does not move, and the half that determines whether the plant runs.

Rotating equipment — pumps, compressors, turbines — gets more attention because it fails more visibly and more often, and because a spare can be swapped in. Static equipment fails rarely and expensively. A heat exchanger with fouled or leaking tubes derates a whole train. A vessel with wall loss found during inspection is a shutdown decision taken under time pressure. A pipeline with integrity findings is a regulatory matter as much as an engineering one.

The economics behind that are stark. Saudi refining capacity runs to more than three million barrels a day, and turnarounds on process units are typically carried out every three to five years. Between those windows the equipment has to be assessed while running, because the alternative is an unplanned outage, and unplanned outages at refinery scale are costed at figures that can exceed $100,000 an hour.

That arithmetic explains the conference programme. Sessions on this equipment class are dominated by inspection, integrity assessment and life extension rather than by new-build design: risk-based inspection, corrosion monitoring, remaining-life calculation, weld repair strategies and the non-destructive examination techniques that let an engineer decide whether a vessel runs to the next turnaround or comes off line now. That decision is where the money is.

The event is also a localisation forum, and it opens in the right province for that. The Eastern Region hosts the fabrication yards at Jubail and Ras Al Khair equipped with heavy lifting, automated welding and non-destructive testing, and it is where the equipment on the programme is both made and used. Aramco confirmed in February 2026 that its in-Kingdom total value add programme had crossed its 70 per cent local content target, with a new ambition of 75 per cent by 2030.

The recent benchmark for what that capability now covers is Zamil Steel's delivery of two gas slug catcher and separator units for Package 4 of the Fadhili Gas Increment Project, each around 1,750 tonnes, with walls 196mm thick clad in Alloy 825 — the first vessels of those specifications fabricated in the Kingdom.

The exhibition is organised by Aldrich International and covers manufacturing and fabrication, power and desalination, and oil, gas and petrochemicals. It runs at Dhahran Expo until 10 September.
